questions.question_hindi:

I. फॉर्म 16 कर्मचारी को उस वित्तीय वर्ष के ठीक बाद वाले वित्तीय वर्ष के 15 जून को या उससे पहले जारी किया जाना चाहिए जिसमें कर की कटौती की गई है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the issuance of Form 16 by an employer/DDO:
I. Form 16 must be issued to the employee annually on or before the 15th of June of the financial year immediately following the financial year in which the tax was deducted.
II. It is mandatory for an employer to issue Form 16 even if the employee's total income is below the taxable exemption limit and no TDS has been deducted.
III. Both Part A and Part B of Form 16 must be generated and downloaded from the TRACES portal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options_english: I only
I and III only
II and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english:
Statements I and III are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.

1. Statement I is correct: Under Rule 31(1) of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, the annual TDS certificate in Form 16 must be furnished to the employee by 15th June of the financial year immediately following the financial year in which the income was paid and tax was deducted (following the filing of the Q4 return in Form 24Q by 31st May).
2. Statement II is incorrect: Under Section 203 of the Income Tax Act, the statutory obligation to issue Form 16 arises only when tax has been deducted at source. If an employee's income is below the basic exemption limit (or no tax is deductible due to rebates) and no TDS has been deducted, issuance of Form 16 is not legally mandatory, though employers may provide a salary statement upon request.
3. Statement III is correct: As per CBDT notifications, deductors must download both Part A and Part B of Form 16 from the TRACES portal to ensure standardization, integrity, and cryptographic QR code authentication.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन II गलत है।

1. कथन I सही है: आयकर नियम, 1962 के नियम 31(1) के तहत, फॉर्म 16 में वार्षिक टीडीएस प्रमाण पत्र कर्मचारी को उस वित्तीय वर्ष के ठीक बाद आने वाले वित्तीय वर्ष के 15 जून तक जारी किया जाना चाहिए जिसमें कर की कटौती की गई है (31 मई तक फॉर्म 24Q में चौथी तिमाही का रिटर्न दाखिल करने के बाद)।
2. कथन II गलत है: आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 203 के तहत, फॉर्म 16 जारी करने की वैधानिक बाध्यता केवल तभी उत्पन्न होती है जब स्रोत पर कर (TDS) काटा गया हो। यदि किसी कर्मचारी की आय मूल कर-मुक्त सीमा से कम है और कोई टीडीएस नहीं काटा गया है, तो फॉर्म 16 जारी करना कानूनन अनिवार्य नहीं है (हालांकि नियोक्ता अनुरोध पर वेतन पर्ची/विवरण दे सकते हैं)।
3. कथन III सही है: सीबीडीटी (CBDT) के निर्देशों के अनुसार, फॉर्म 16 के मानकीकरण और प्रामाणिकता के लिए भाग A और भाग B दोनों को ट्रेसेस (TRACES) पोर्टल से डाउनलोड किया जाना आवश्यक है।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I and III only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Form 16 must be issued by the employer by June fifteenth following the relevant financial year, and both Part A and Part B must be downloaded from the TRACES portal. Issuing Form 16 is required when tax is deducted; if income is below taxable limits and no tax is deducted, issuing it is optional.

questions.question_english: What is meant by a "Nil TDS Return" in the context of statutory tax compliance by a Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO)?
options_english: A return filed by an educational institution that does not possess a valid PAN or TAN
A return filed when an employee claims a complete refund of tax deducted during the year
A quarterly TDS statement filed by a deductor declaring zero tax deduction during the relevant quarter
A special tax return filed exclusively by non-profit educational or charitable organizations
questions.explanation_english: A "Nil TDS Return" refers to a quarterly tax statement submitted by a registered deductor (such as a school DDO having a TAN) indicating that no tax was deducted at source during that specific quarter. This situation typically arises when payments made to deductees or employees fall below statutory tax thresholds (e.g., employee salaries remaining within the basic exemption limit under Section 192, or vendor payments within the Section 194C threshold). While deductors can also file a 'Declaration for non-filing of TDS return' via TRACES if no taxable payments occurred, in statutory practice, submitting a quarterly statement declaring zero deduction confirms that the deductor was operational and had zero tax liability to remit for that quarter.
questions.explanation_hindi: "शून्य टीडीएस विवरणी" (Nil TDS Return) से तात्पर्य किसी पंजीकृत कटौतीकर्ता (जैसे टैन धारक विद्यालय का DDO) द्वारा दाखिल किए जाने वाले ऐसे त्रैमासिक विवरण से है, जिसमें यह प्रमाणित किया जाता है कि संबंधित तिमाही के दौरान स्रोत पर कोई कर कटौती (TDS) नहीं की गई है। ऐसी स्थिति सामान्यतः तब उत्पन्न होती है जब कर्मचारियों या संविदाकारों को किए गए भुगतान निर्धारित कर-योग्य सीमा से नीचे रहते हैं (जैसे धारा 192 के तहत कर्मचारियों का वेतन मूल छूट सीमा से कम होना या धारा 194C की सीमा के भीतर होना)। यद्यपि कटौतीकर्ता TRACES पर विवरणी दाखिल न करने का घोषणा-पत्र भी दे सकते हैं, किन्तु शून्य कटौती दर्शाने वाला यह विवरण यह पुष्ट करता है कि उक्त तिमाही के लिए कटौतीकर्ता की कोई टीडीएस देनदारी नहीं थी। अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Donations made by a teacher to the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF) are eligible for a 100% deduction without any qualifying limit under Section 80G of the Income Tax Act.
Reason (R): To claim a deduction under Section 80G, the donation can be made in cash irrespective of the amount.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is true: Under Section 80G(1)(i) read with Section 80G(2)(a)(iiia) of the Income Tax Act, contributions made to the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF) qualify for a 100% tax deduction without any upper qualifying limit (unlike donations to general private charitable trusts which are restricted to 50% deduction subject to a 10% ceiling of Adjusted Gross Total Income).
Reason (R) is false: Under Section 80G(5D) of the Income Tax Act, no deduction is permissible in respect of any donation exceeding ₹2,000 unless such sum is paid by any mode other than cash (such as account payee cheque, demand draft, NEFT/RTGS, UPI, or net banking). Cash donations exceeding ₹2,000 are strictly disallowed in toto.
Therefore, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) सही है: आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 80G के अंतर्गत प्रधानमंत्री राष्ट्रीय राहत कोष (PMNRF) में किया गया दान बिना किसी अर्हक सीमा (Qualifying Limit) के 100% कर कटौती के लिए पात्र है।
कारण (R) गलत है: धारा 80G(5D) के सांविधिक प्रावधानों के तहत, ₹2,000 से अधिक का कोई भी नकद दान आयकर कटौती के लिए पूर्णतः अमान्य है। यदि दान ₹2,000 से अधिक है, तो कटौती का लाभ प्राप्त करने के लिए उसका भुगतान बैंकिंग चैनलों (जैसे चेक, ड्राफ्ट, एनईएफटी, यूपीआई आदि) के माध्यम से किया जाना अनिवार्य है।
अतः (A) सही है परंतु (R) गलत है।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) A is true but R is false

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Donations made to the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund qualify for a one hundred percent deduction without qualifying limits under Section 80G. However, under Section 80G(5D), cash donations exceeding two thousand rupees are strictly disallowed as deductions, requiring contributions above this limit to be made through non-cash banking channels.

questions.question_english: Under Section 80B(5) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, the term "Gross Total Income" (GTI) is best defined as:
options_english: The total salary received including all exempt allowances before standard deduction.
The final taxable income on which tax liability is computed.
The net income computed after allowing all statutory exemptions and Chapter VI-A deductions.
Total income computed under the five heads of income before allowing Chapter VI-A deductions.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 80B(5) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, 'Gross Total Income' (GTI) is explicitly defined as the aggregate total of income computed in accordance with the provisions of the Act under all five heads of income:
1. Income from Salaries (Sections 15 to 17)
2. Income from House Property (Sections 22 to 27)
3. Profits and Gains of Business or Profession (Sections 28 to 44DB)
4. Capital Gains (Sections 45 to 55A)
5. Income from Other Sources (Sections 56 to 59)
—after giving effect to clubbing provisions (Sections 60 to 65) and set-off and carry forward of losses (Sections 70 to 80), but BEFORE allowing any deductions under Chapter VI-A of the Act (such as Sections 80C, 80D, 80E, 80G, etc.). After deducting Chapter VI-A deductions from Gross Total Income, the resulting figure is 'Total Income' (or Net Taxable Income) defined under Section 2(45).
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 80B(5) के अनुसार, 'सकल कुल आय' (Gross Total Income / GTI) को आयकर के पांचों शीर्षों के अंतर्गत अधिनियम के प्रावधानों के अनुसार गणना की गई आय के कुल योग के रूप में परिभाषित किया गया है:
1. वेतन से आय
2. मकान संपत्ति से आय
3. व्यवसाय या पेशे से लाभ एवं अभिलाभ
4. पूंजीगत अभिलाभ
5. अन्य स्रोतों से आय
इसमें हानियों के समायोजन (सेट-ऑफ) के बाद की आय शामिल होती है, परंतु इसमें अध्याय VI-A (जैसे धारा 80C, 80D, 80E, 80G आदि) के तहत मिलने वाली किसी भी कटौती को घटाने से पहले की स्थिति होती है। जब सकल कुल आय में से अध्याय VI-A की कटौतियां घटा दी जाती हैं, तो प्राप्त राशि को धारा 2(45) के तहत 'कुल आय' (Total Taxable Income) कहा जाता है जिस पर कर लगाया जाता है। अतः विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।
questions.topic: Income Tax and GST Basics for School Administration
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Total income under five heads before Chapter VI-A deductions.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: VI-A deductions. Under Section 80B(5) of the Income Tax Act, Gross Total Income is defined as the aggregate total of income computed under all five heads of income--Salaries, House Property, Business/ Profession, Capital Gains, and Other Sources-- before allowing any tax deductions under Chapter VI-A of the Act.

questions.question_english: What is the maximum amount of Standard Deduction available to a salaried employee under Section 16(ia) of the Income Tax Act for the Financial Year 2023-24 (Assessment Year 2024-25)?
questions.question_hindi: वित्तीय वर्ष 2023-24 (कर निर्धारण वर्ष 2024-25) के लिए आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 16(ia) के तहत एक वेतनभोगी कर्मचारी को मिलने वाली मानक कटौती (Standard Deduction) की अधिकतम राशि क्या है?
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 16(ia) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, a salaried individual (or a pensioner) is entitled to a standard deduction from gross salary of up to ₹50,000 or the amount of the salary, whichever is less, for the Financial Year 2023-24 (Assessment Year 2024-25). This flat statutory deduction was reintroduced by the Finance Act 2018 (initially at ₹40,000 and enhanced to ₹50,000 by Finance (No. 2) Act 2019). It is allowed automatically without requiring any investment proof, bills, or actual expenditure receipts. (Note: The Finance Act 2024 later enhanced this deduction to ₹75,000 under the New Tax Regime, but only with effect from FY 2024-25 / AY 2025-26).
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 16(ia) के तहत वित्तीय वर्ष 2023-24 (कर निर्धारण वर्ष 2024-25) के लिए वेतनभोगी कर्मचारियों और पेंशनभोगियों को उनके सकल वेतन से ₹50,000 या वेतन की वास्तविक राशि (जो भी कम हो) की मानक कटौती (Standard Deduction) प्रदान की जाती है। यह कटौती वित्त अधिनियम 2018 द्वारा पुनः प्रारंभ की गई थी (शुरुआत में ₹40,000, जिसे 2019 में बढ़ाकर ₹50,000 किया गया)। इस कटौती का दावा करने के लिए किसी व्यय बिल या रसीद की आवश्यकता नहीं होती। (ध्यान दें कि वित्त अधिनियम 2024 द्वारा नई कर व्यवस्था में इसे बढ़ाकर ₹75,000 किया गया है, किंतु वह वित्तीय वर्ष 2024-25 से प्रभावी है)।

questions.question_hindi:

questions.question_english:
Consider the following retirement terminal benefits and their tax exemptions applicable to government employees under the Income Tax Act:
I. Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity (DCRG) is fully exempt from income tax for government employees.
II. Leave encashment received at the time of retirement is fully exempt from income tax for government employees.
III. Commuted value of pension received upon retirement is fully exempt from income tax for government employees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 10 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, statutory retirement benefits received by Central Government, State Government, and local authority employees enjoy comprehensive and unlimited tax exemptions:
1. Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity (DCRG): Fully exempt under Section 10(10)(i) without any monetary ceiling.
2. Leave Encashment: Under Section 10(10AA)(i), any payment received by government employees as leave encashment at the time of retirement/superannuation is entirely exempt from income tax without any monetary cap.
3. Commuted Pension: Under Section 10(10A)(i), any payment in commutation of pension received by government employees under the Civil Pensions (Commutation) Rules is 100% exempt from income tax.
Because all three statements (I, II, and III) are accurate, Option D is the correct choice.

2. धारा 10(10AA)(i): सरकारी कर्मचारियों को सेवानिवृत्ति या अधिवर्षिता के समय प्राप्त अवकाश नकदीकरण (लीव इनकैशमेंट) बिना किसी मौद्रिक सीमा के पूर्णतः कर-मुक्त है।
3. धारा 10(10A)(i): सरकारी कर्मचारियों द्वारा प्राप्त पेंशन का रूपांतरित मूल्य (कम्यूटेड पेंशन) आयकर से 100% मुक्त होता है।

II. Every person liable to deduct tax at source (TDS) is statutorily required to obtain a TAN under Section 203A of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
III. A Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) can use their personal PAN instead of the school's TAN for depositing employee TDS.
IV. The same TAN can be used for both Tax Deduction at Source (TDS) and Tax Collection at Source (TCS) compliances.

options_english: I, II, and III only

II, III, and IV only

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 203A of the Income Tax Act, 1961, every person deducting or collecting tax at source must apply for and obtain a 10-digit alphanumeric TAN issued by the Income Tax Department (Statements I and II are correct). Statement III is completely incorrect: a DDO or deductor can never use their personal PAN in lieu of the official TAN. Mixing personal PAN with organizational TDS deposits leads to severe reconciliation mismatch and attracts statutory penalties under Section 272BB of the Income Tax Act (penalty of ₹10,000). Therefore, statements I, II, and IV only are correct.

questions.question_english: Which of the following forms is the comprehensive annual tax credit statement maintained by the Income Tax Department that displays taxes deducted at source (TDS) on behalf of a taxpayer by all deductors across the financial year?

Form 16B
Form 26AS
Form 15G
questions.explanation_english:
Form 26AS is the consolidated Annual Tax Statement generated by the Income Tax Department under Section 203AA read with Rule 31AB for every PAN holder.

Form 26AS provides a comprehensive record of:
1. Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) by employers (salaries) and other deductors (contractors, bank interest, professional fees).
2. Tax Collected at Source (TCS) by sellers.
3. Advance tax and self-assessment tax paid directly by the taxpayer.
4. Details of income tax refunds received during the financial year.
5. Specified Financial Transactions (SFT) reported by banks and financial institutions.

Other forms:
- Form 12BA: Statement showing perquisites and other fringe benefits provided to an employee.
- Form 16B: TDS certificate for tax deducted under Section 194-IA on the purchase of immovable property.
- Form 15G: Self-declaration form to claim exemption from TDS on interest income by individuals below 60 years.
questions.explanation_hindi:
फॉर्म 26AS प्रत्येक पैन धारक के लिए आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 203AA और नियम 31AB के तहत आयकर विभाग द्वारा तैयार किया जाने वाला समेकित वार्षिक कर विवरण (Annual Tax Statement) है।

फॉर्म 26AS में निम्नलिखित का व्यापक रिकॉर्ड होता है:
1. नियोक्ताओं (वेतन) तथा अन्य कटौतीकर्ताओं (ठेकेदारों, बैंक ब्याज, व्यावसायिक शुल्क आदि) द्वारा काटा गया स्रोत पर कर (TDS)।
2. विक्रेताओं द्वारा स्रोत पर संगृहीत कर (TCS)।
3. करदाता द्वारा सीधे जमा किया गया अग्रिम कर (Advance Tax) और स्व-निर्धारण कर (Self-Assessment Tax)।
4. वित्तीय वर्ष के दौरान प्राप्त आयकर रिफंड का विवरण।
5. बैंकों और वित्तीय संस्थानों द्वारा रिपोर्ट किए गए निर्दिष्ट वित्तीय लेनदेन (SFT)।

Under RCM, however, the recipient (buyer/service receiver) must directly compute and pay the tax into the government account via electronic cash ledger. questions.explanation_english: Under the Income Tax Act, 1961, a Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) is merely a tax deductor, not an assessing officer. Determining, evaluating, or auditing the overall annual taxable profits and corporate tax liabilities of external third-party vendors (such as mid-day meal caterers) is the exclusive statutory function of the jurisdictional Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO), completely outside the scope of a school DDO.

questions.question_english: A retired school Principal draws a regular monthly pension of ₹40,000 from the government, which is assessed to income tax under the head "Salaries". Is the retired Principal entitled to the Standard Deduction of ₹50,000 under Section 16(ia)?
questions.question_hindi: एक सेवानिवृत्त स्कूल प्रधानाचार्य सरकार से ₹40,000 प्रति माह की नियमित पेंशन प्राप्त करते हैं, जिस पर "वेतन" शीर्षक के तहत आयकर लगाया जाता है। क्या सेवानिवृत्त प्रधानाचार्य धारा 16(ia) के तहत ₹50,000 की मानक कटौती (Standard Deduction) पाने के हकदार हैं?
options_english: No, because the standard deduction under Section 16(ia) is strictly reserved for active serving employees.
Yes, but the deduction is limited to ₹15,000 or one-third of the pension, whichever is less.
Yes, the pensioner is entitled to the full flat standard deduction of ₹50,000 against their pension income.
No, pensioners are eligible only for interest deduction under Section 80TTB and not salary deductions.
options_hindi: नहीं, क्योंकि धारा 16(ia) के तहत मानक कटौती केवल वर्तमान में कार्यरत सेवारत कर्मचारियों के लिए आरक्षित है।
हाँ, लेकिन कटौती ₹15,000 या पेंशन के एक-तिहाई (जो भी कम हो) तक ही सीमित है।

नहीं, पेंशनभोगी केवल धारा 80TTB के तहत ब्याज कटौती के पात्र हैं, वेतन कटौती के नहीं।
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 17(1)(ii) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, any pension received by an individual from their former employer (including government or school administration) is legally classified as 'salary'. As per Section 16(ia), standard deduction is available from income chargeable under the head 'Salaries'. The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) through Circular No. 01/2019 and clarificatory notifications specifically clarified that pensioners drawing regular monthly pension are fully entitled to claim the flat standard deduction up to ₹50,000 (or the actual pension amount, whichever is less) under Section 16(ia). (Note that the 1/3rd or ₹15,000 limit applies only to 'Family Pension' under Section 57(iia), not to regular employee pension).
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 17(1)(ii) के अनुसार, पूर्व नियोक्ता (सरकार या विद्यालय प्रबंधन) से प्राप्त होने वाली नियमित पेंशन को 'वेतन' (Salary) माना जाता है। धारा 16(ia) के तहत मानक कटौती 'वेतन' शीर्षक के अंतर्गत कर-योग्य किसी भी आय से स्वीकार्य होती है। केंद्रीय प्रत्यक्ष कर बोर्ड (CBDT) ने स्पष्ट किया है कि नियमित पेंशन पाने वाले सभी सेवानिवृत्त कर्मचारी धारा 16(ia) के तहत ₹50,000 (या वास्तविक पेंशन राशि, जो भी कम हो) की एकमुश्त मानक कटौती पाने के पूर्ण हकदार हैं। (ध्यान रहे कि एक-तिहाई या ₹15,000 की सीमा धारा 57(iia) के तहत 'पारिवारिक पेंशन' पर लागू होती है, कर्मचारी की स्वयं की पेंशन पर नहीं)।

Assertion (A): Professional tax deducted from the salary of an employee by the employer is allowed as a statutory deduction from gross salary under Section 16(iii) of the Income Tax Act.
Reason (R): The Constitution of India empowers state governments and local authorities to levy taxes on professions, trades, callings, and employments.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is true: Under Section 16(iii) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, tax on employment (commonly known as Professional Tax) levied by or under any State law is allowable as a statutory deduction from gross salary in the financial year in which it is actually paid.
Reason (R) is true: Article 276 of the Constitution of India provides constitutional authority to State Legislatures and local municipal authorities to levy taxes for the benefit of the State on professions, trades, callings, and employments (subject to a maximum ceiling of ₹2,500 per person per annum).
Because Professional Tax is a distinct constitutional levy imposed directly on employment under Article 276, the Income Tax Act in Section 16(iii) specifically provides a deduction for this State tax so that an employee is not taxed on money already paid to the State under constitutional authority. Thus, Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) सही है: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 16(iii) के तहत, किसी राज्य विधि के अंतर्गत कर्मचारी के वेतन से काटा और चुकाया गया व्यावसायिक कर (प्रोफेशनल टैक्स) 'वेतन से आय' की गणना करते समय वास्तविक भुगतान के आधार पर सकल वेतन से कटौती योग्य होता है।

चूंकि व्यावसायिक कर राज्य द्वारा अनुच्छेद 276 के तहत रोजगार पर लगाया गया एक अनिवार्य संवैधानिक कर है, इसलिए केंद्र सरकार ने वेतनभोगी कर्मचारियों को दोहरे कराधान से राहत देने हेतु आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 16(iii) में इसकी कटौती का स्पष्ट प्रावधान किया है। अतः (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।

questions.question_english: A Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) estimates the annual income of a teacher and deducts TDS on a monthly basis. In the month of January, the teacher submits documentary proofs of tax-saving investments (under Chapter VI-A) that were previously declared in April but not documented. What is the legally prescribed course of action for the DDO?
options_english: Reject the proofs outright because they were not submitted in April at the beginning of the financial year.
Instruct the teacher to claim a refund directly from the Income Tax Department while continuing TDS deduction at the earlier rate.
Re-calculate the total estimated tax liability using the verified proofs and adjust the remaining monthly TDS deductions accordingly.
Immediately refund the excess TDS deducted so far directly to the employee from the school's contingency fund.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 192(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, the DDO has the legal authority to adjust any excess or deficiency in TDS deductions across subsequent months of the financial year.

Key administrative procedures:
1. At the beginning of the financial year (April/May), employees submit an investment declaration based on which estimated TDS is deducted on an average monthly rate.
2. Around December/January, employees submit actual documentary evidence and payment receipts (e.g., PPF, LIC, ELSS, tuition fees under Section 80C, mediclaim under Section 80D).
3. Upon receiving verified proofs, the DDO re-computes the employee's total annual taxable income and tax liability.
4. The DDO then adjusts the remaining tax to be deducted in equal installments over the remaining months (January, February, and March).

The DDO cannot refund TDS from school funds because deducted tax has already been credited to the Central Government.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 192(3) के तहत, DDO को वित्तीय वर्ष के शेष महीनों में टीडीएस कटौती में किसी भी अधिकता या कमी को समायोजित करने का वैधानिक अधिकार प्राप्त है।

प्रमुख प्रशासनिक प्रक्रियाएँ:
1. वित्तीय वर्ष के प्रारंभ (अप्रैल/मई) में, कर्मचारी एक निवेश घोषणा प्रस्तुत करते हैं जिसके आधार पर औसत मासिक दर से अनुमानित टीडीएस काटा जाता है।
2. दिसंबर/जनवरी के आसपास, कर्मचारी वास्तविक दस्तावेजी साक्ष्य और रसीदें (जैसे पीपीएफ, एलआईसी, ईएलएसएस, धारा 80C के तहत ट्यूशन फीस, धारा 80D के तहत मेडिक्लेम) जमा करते हैं।
3. सत्यापित साक्ष्य प्राप्त होने पर, DDO कर्मचारी की कुल वार्षिक कर योग्य आय और कर देयता की पुनर्गणना करता है।
4. इसके बाद DDO शेष महीनों (जनवरी, फरवरी और मार्च) के दौरान काटे जाने वाले शेष कर को समान किस्तों में समायोजित करता है।

DDO स्कूल फंड से टीडीएस रिफंड नहीं कर सकता क्योंकि काटा गया कर पहले ही केंद्र सरकार के खाते में जमा कराया जा चुका होता है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding statutory Form 12BA under the Income Tax Rules, 1962:
I. It is a statement showing particulars of perquisites, other fringe benefits or amenities, and profits in lieu of salary.
II. It is mandatory for the employer to issue Form 12BA if the monetary salary paid or payable to the employee exceeds ₹1,50,000 in a financial year.
III. It must be issued along with and annexed to Form 16 (Part B).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 26A(2) of the Income-tax Rules, 1962:
1. Form 12BA is a statutory statement containing complete particulars of perquisites, other fringe benefits or amenities, and profits in lieu of salary provided to an employee.
2. Threshold: Form 12BA is mandatory where the salary paid or payable to the employee exceeds ₹1,50,000 in a financial year. If salary is up to ₹1,50,000, perquisite details are simply entered within Form 16 itself.
3. Issuance: Form 12BA must accompany and be annexed to Form 16 when issued to the employee by the statutory deadline of 15th June.
Because all three statements (I, II, and III) are accurate, Option D is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर नियम, 1962 के नियम 26A(2) के अनुसार:
1. फॉर्म 12BA एक वैधानिक विवरण-पत्र है जिसमें कर्मचारी को प्रदान किए गए अनुलाभों (Perquisites), सुविधाओं तथा वेतन के बदले लाभों (Profits in lieu of salary) का विस्तृत ब्यौरा होता है।
2. वित्तीय सीमा: यदि किसी कर्मचारी का वित्तीय वर्ष में देय मौद्रिक वेतन ₹1,50,000 से अधिक है, तो नियोक्ता द्वारा फॉर्म 12BA जारी करना अनिवार्य होता है। (यदि वेतन ₹1,50,000 से कम हो तो अनुलाभों का विवरण फॉर्म 16 में ही दिया जा सकता है)।
3. संलग्नता: फॉर्म 12BA को फॉर्म 16 (पार्ट B) के साथ संलग्न करके कर्मचारी को 15 जून तक उपलब्ध कराया जाना आवश्यक है।
अतः कथन I, II और III तीनों सही हैं।

questions.question_english: A government school procures examination printing services worth ₹60,000 from a commercial vendor. The vendor fails to furnish a valid Permanent Account Number (PAN) to the school's DDO. In accordance with Section 206AA of the Income Tax Act, 1961, at what rate must the DDO deduct TDS?
options_english: 1% flat rate on the total contract value
2% flat rate on the total contract value
10% flat rate on the aggregate invoice value
20% or the applicable statutory rate, whichever is higher
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 206AA of the Income Tax Act, 1961, any person entitled to receive any sum or income on which tax is deductible at source (the deductee) must furnish their Permanent Account Number (PAN) to the deductor (the DDO).
If the deductee fails to furnish their PAN, the tax must be deducted at the highest of the following rates:
1. At the rate specified in the relevant provision of the Act (for contractual printing under Section 194C, normally 1% for individual/HUF and 2% for others);
2. At the rate or rates in force; or
3. At the rate of twenty per cent (20%).
Therefore, because 20% is higher than the standard 1% or 2% rate under Section 194C, the DDO is legally bound to withhold tax at 20% or the applicable rate, whichever is higher.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 206AA के अनुसार, जिस व्यक्ति को ऐसा कोई भुगतान प्राप्त होना है जिस पर स्रोत पर कर कटौती (TDS) देय है, उसके लिए कटौतीकर्ता (DDO) को अपना स्थायी खाता संख्या (PAN) प्रस्तुत करना अनिवार्य है।
यदि प्राप्तकर्ता अपना पैन प्रस्तुत करने में विफल रहता है, तो DDO को निम्नलिखित में से जो भी उच्चतम हो, उस दर से टीडीएस काटना होगा:
1. अधिनियम के संबंधित प्रावधान में विनिर्दिष्ट दर पर (धारा 194C के तहत मुद्रण अनुबंध पर सामान्य दर व्यष्टि/HUF के लिए 1% और अन्य के लिए 2% है);
2. लागू वित्त अधिनियम में प्रभावी दर पर; अथवा
3. बीस प्रतिशत (20%) की दर पर।
अतः DDO को 20% या लागू दर, जो भी अधिक हो, पर टीडीएस काटना अनिवार्य है।

questions.question_english: By what date must an employer or DDO typically deposit the TDS deducted from employee salaries into the Central Government account for the months from April to February?
options_english: On or before the 7th of the following month
On or before the 15th of the following month
On or before the 30th of the following month
By the 31st of March of that financial year
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 30(2) of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, tax deducted at source must be deposited to the credit of the Central Government according to the following statutory schedule:

1. For deductions made from April to February: On or before the 7th day of the month immediately following the month of deduction (e.g., TDS deducted from salary paid in October must be deposited by 7th November).
2. For deductions made in March: On or before the 30th day of April of the subsequent financial year.
3. Government offices depositing tax through book adjustment (without an income-tax challan): The tax must be credited on the very same day the deduction is made.

Failure to deposit by the 7th of the following month attracts interest under Section 201(1A) at 1.5% per month or part of a month.
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर नियम, 1962 के नियम 30(2) के अनुसार, स्रोत पर काटे गए कर (TDS) को निम्नलिखित वैधानिक समय सारणी के अनुसार केंद्र सरकार के खाते में जमा किया जाना चाहिए:

1. अप्रैल से फरवरी तक के महीनों में की गई कटौती के लिए: कटौती के महीने के ठीक बाद वाले महीने की 7 तारीख को या उससे पहले (उदाहरण के लिए, अक्टूबर माह के वेतन से काटा गया टीडीएस 7 नवंबर तक जमा होना चाहिए)।
2. मार्च माह में की गई कटौती के लिए: अगले वित्तीय वर्ष के 30 अप्रैल को या उससे पहले।
3. सरकारी कार्यालय जहाँ बिना आयकर चालान के बुक एडजस्टमेंट (Book Entry) द्वारा कर जमा किया जाता है: कर कटौती वाले दिन ही जमा किया जाना अनिवार्य है।

अगले महीने की 7 तारीख तक जमा न करने पर धारा 201(1A) के तहत 1.5% प्रति माह या माह के किसी भाग की दर से ब्याज देय होता है।
